utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Good morning to everybody. May we hear the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, with Ruth Karper for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we start with today's witness, we have two urgent matters to discuss related to the upcoming witness 058. The Defence wants to have the transcript of the former hearing of this witness. Correct? For these purposes, we need under Rule 75(F) to (H) a formal request in order that we can forward this, and it will be only possible if we take your request now to the transcript, and based on this, we'll try to do our very best that we have the transcripts available. May we, therefore, hear your request, if any.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. We will formally wish to make a request pursuant to the Rules that the transcript of Witness 058 be permitted to be distributed to the Defence counsel and to the OTP. It was our understanding initially that this witness did not testify in a closed session. Subsequently, we learned that that was an error, that he testified in a closed session in the Keraterm Sikirica case. And therefore, we would be asking that that transcript be submitted to the Defence counsel for our review and necessary preparation of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Any comments by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we already have given the Defence the transcript. We understood this was a witness under the Rules. We thought that under the new Rule, we no longer are required when a witness is going to appear in another case and has indicated he will appear to ask for the consent of the witness or the Trial Chamber to disclose the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: What we learned until now is that in fact the witness was heard in closed session, and even under the new Rules applicable as of I think July or August last year, we need to contact the Judge of the earlier case, in this case, Judge Robinson. So therefore, to be on the safe side, there are no objections from your side. So then we can proceed on this basis. And the second point is we received yesterday a motion from the Defence related to two witnesses, a request for subpoena. First, the Trial Chamber does not believe that it's necessary to subpoena this witness. The most expeditious way in order to call this witness is, from our point of view, to call these witnesses as Chamber witnesses, also taking into account that we learned from the Defence that those witnesses would not appear or would not be prepared to appear as witnesses by the Defence. Nevertheless, I think it's no doubt that the Defence has shown good cause to hear these witnesses. Therefore, we would intend to proceed this way, calling these witnesses as Chamber witnesses but as in the beginning without subpoena.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That would be acceptable with the Defence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any comments by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Just for future reference on the last issue, it was our understanding under Rule 75(E)(ii), that we were obligated to provide this type of transcript. Obviously, this was a Defence witness, and the Defence believe this would mitigate guilt in some way. And the Rules simply require us to notify the Defence of any protective measures in the earlier proceeding. That's how we're interpreting it and just -- I just bring that up so that we can be informed if the Court has a different interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. We've got your point, and from this we learned that in any event, the Defence has no prejudice from these proceedings, and we would appreciate also to have access to these transcripts. We try to do our best, but as we said earlier, following contacts with the other Chamber, we thought this would be necessary to have this formal approach. Thank you. Then related to the second matter, the request by the Defence to hear two additional witnesses and to summon them as Chamber witnesses during the Defence case is hereby granted. We'll do the necessary and inform the parties as soon as possible about the outcome of our attempt. The witness of today has asked for protective measures. They have to be justified, but they can only be justified when the witness is here and in the courtroom. To be on the safe side, if there are no objections, we want to start in closed session to hear the submission of this witness related to the protective measures. And may I ask for additional precaution in case we have only voice and face distortion. So Madam Registrar, we are in closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For a few minutes. I learned during the break that there would be a change in the order of calling the witnesses by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. We were informed by the witness and victims unit that one of our witnesses has been -- either come down with the flu or is ill. And so instead of proceeding with Witness Number 058, we would proceed in I guess any order that the OTP would like, with either Witness 071 or Witness 072. Since I know they mentioned there may have been a scheduling issue with some binders they were compiling on the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The consequent logical order would be immediately to hear Witness 72. But I don't want to anticipate the answer by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We actually would have a request -- or I would have a request that we do Witness 71. I can't be here for tomorrow, so I would like to see Witness 72 myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think you are prepared for both witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We are. But I have just been informed that we also thought logically would go, so I informed the witness and victim unit protection, whatever, that 72 would come first. So as long as we can get some assistance from the Court in rescheduling that, we are prepared with either one. We also thought it might have been a preference, and we took an informed decision and scheduled 72. But I'm sure with the Court's assistance, we could get that clarified in the next hour or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I will not promise anything in advance. And I don't know whether or not there are impediments. But I think we handled this also in the past whenever the Defence asked for another order for reasons that the one or other counsel could not be present. So therefore we should be in agreement that we start with 71 tomorrow. But of course, we can't exclude that we may even start with Witness 72 tomorrow. May I ask, Witness 58, he is ill, I learned this. But he's in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That is my understanding, Your Honour. We haven't been able to meet or visit with him, but that is the information that was provided to us with the representative with the unit. We hope to accomplish that in the next hour or to what the issues are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I would appreciate if you could let me know today, and if of course, if it should be ex parte, then we would immediately inform the other party about this issue. No doubt about this. In case Witness 58 would not be available, do you have a reserve witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We did try that, and regretfully to report, it's impossible because of the timing of various procedural things such as obtaining visas, length of time for visas. So we do not. We are required to at least give five days' notice at a minimum, and then I think they only have temporary entrance permits or visas to come in and then leave within a specific time period as opposed to a longer period. But we are trying to do everything we can, but as of this moment we would not have any other witnesses. But we do believe that the remaining 71 and 72 will take slightly longer than the anticipated time that we reference in our proffer. Not significantly longer, but perhaps two and a half to three hours on each, as opposed to the initial estimate of approximately two hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. So please inform us immediately if you know whether there is at least a likelihood that Witness 58 will be able to appear. And there is one additional question: Unfortunately once again related to this legal system prevailing here. I took it that the transcripts on the previous testimony given on Keraterm was already disclosed to the other side. If I'm not totally wrong, the same witness testified as well in Omarska case. So for us apparently, it's not available. It's not on the Internet. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We did provide. We just provided this afternoon copies to the Chambers and the Defence. Apparently the Chamber will make -- the legal officer indicated copies would be made for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So we did what we could in the meantime in order to have -- to be on the safe side and have the consent if necessary. Rule 75 is one of the worst Rules we have in our Rules of Procedure and Evidence by the Judges, so this shouldn't be an obstacle. But I just learned that Witness 58 is travelling home tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll check. I mean, we were here the entire day, so we will accomplish and report to the Court everything I know. I have not talked to the witness, and we have not consulted or met. So as soon as we find out, we'll inform the Court and the parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Any other issues for the moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well there is one other, if I may, but I'm not sure if it's appropriate now or at a subsequent time. It involves questions put to the witness and witnesses by the OTP, specifically on page 83, line 11, and page 103, line 11. All I'm looking for from the Chamber is clarification if the OTP can put suggestive questions as they have throughout without showing a basis to the Court or the parties, we would merely request that the Defence be given that same opportunity. At each time the Defence asked a question about an article or about a statement by another party, the Court respectfully, even without the interruption and objection by the OTP, would say or request the page number, the document that we're referencing, and in this instance, although with other witnesses as well, we felt there was a practice established that you must, when you discuss items such as whether an individual was a member of the Markovic party or whether or not this witness that the Court called was alleged by some of their witnesses to be present and working at Omarska, or is it simply just speculation on their part in an attempt to have the witness become distraught or whatever their strategy is, give us that evidence. Give it to us beforehand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Once again, first you should read carefully today's transcript, and you will immediately identify that I asked the OTP as well to indicate clearly the transcript page they are making reference to. As regards other documents, in this set, it is impossible for the Judges to know what the parties know. So therefore, it might be that based on the one or other exhibit available, made available only for the other party, the other party has reason to know that the question has a sound basis. If not, please object, and then we have to ask the questioning party what is the basis for this answer. It's as simple as that. So therefore, I only can ask you when necessary to intervene. Otherwise, I take it that you have the same information, and it's among the parties undisputed. Anything else?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: From the side of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: There is on the -- it doesn't have to be discussed today, given the hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the interest of all participants, it's a good decision. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 22nd day of January, 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.39 p.m.,
